title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
layout_note: Left: the input photo, the frozen image encoder and the Q-Former in a tinted region with its three objectives on top. Right, behind a thin vertical rule: one small attention-mask diagram per objective with a key at its top.
grouping: The Q-Former is a pale-yellow tinted region; the right half is set off by a vertical rule; each mask diagram has its objective name in a box below it.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded boxes in saturated fills per layer type; the frozen encoder a blue trapezoid with a snowflake; masks as small grids with grey cells.
proposed_highlight: The proposed Q-Former is the tinted region; the three objectives are boxes on its top edge, each explained by its mask on the right.
lesson: When several objectives differ only in what each token may see, draw one small mask grid per objective beside the model rather than describing it in the boxes.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue ICML 2023 (not verified in this session). Card written while studying arrangement (2026-11-15).

arrangement.units: the model on the left (tinted region), the per-objective mask panel on the right behind a thin vertical rule
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo at the left edge; the input text as a quoted card under the text branch
arrangement.losses_at: the three objectives on top of the model; repeated under their masks on the right

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: one Q-Former region holds a query tower and a text tower whose self-attention layers are joined, and three objective boxes sit above both towers, each objective's self-attention mask drawn as a 4x4 Q/T grid in a separate panel to the right

relations.form: input photo -> frozen blue Image Encoder trapezoid -> Q-Former left to right, then bottom-to-top inside each tower (Self Attention -> Cross Attention -> Feed Forward, xN)

the two towers' Self Attention blocks are linked by three labelled horizontal arrows (bidirectional, multimodal causal, uni-modal, the last crossed out) under an 'Attention Masking' heading, and all three objective boxes draw from both towers' tops
image features enter the query tower's Cross Attention block from the side with the side label 'for every other block'
right panel, behind a thin vertical rule: three mask grids side by side, each with its objective's salmon box repeated beneath it
each objective is shown as a mask over the Q and T token positions (grey = masked cells in a Q/T-labelled grid), keyed above

channels.colour: blue = frozen image encoder (with snowflake), pale yellow region = the trainable Q-Former, salmon = objectives, block fills (orange self-attention, grey cross-attention, purple/green feed-forward) = layer type, with feed-forward coloured differently per tower; small coloured squares = learned queries; grey/white mask cells keyed as masked/unmasked
channels.shape: trapezoid = encoder, rounded rectangles = layers and objectives, rounded tray of squares = queries, quoted pill = input text
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; a dashed crossed-out arrow = blocked uni-modal attention
channels.frame: the yellow region frames the Q-Former; a thin outline groups each tower's xN stack; a vertical rule separates the mask panel

quality.strengths: Objectives are tied to their masks by repeating the same salmon box under each grid, so the reader sees how one module serves three objectives; the input image and the quoted sentence are drawn as data; the frozen encoder is marked by colour plus snowflake.
quality.weaknesses: In the left panel the three objectives sit as boxes above the towers with lines merging into them, so the compared representations (query output vs text [CLS]) are not drawn; the attention-masking types are text labels on arrows between the towers, duplicating the mask panel; feed-forward colours differ between towers without a stated meaning.

insights.structure: Left half: input photo -> blue frozen Image Encoder trapezoid -> a pale-yellow 'Q-Former' region holding two side-by-side transformer towers (query and text) with three objective boxes above; right half, set off by a vertical rule, is a row of three mask diagrams each with its objective box beneath.
insights.data: The image is a real cat photo split into grid patches; learned queries are a row of small coloured squares in a rounded box; the text is a quoted sentence 'a cat wearing sunglasses'; attention masks are 4×4 grids of white/grey cells labelled Q and T.
insights.emphasis: The Q-Former is the only tinted region, the frozen image encoder carries a snowflake, and the three objectives (Image-Text Matching, Contrastive Learning, Image-Grounded Text Generation) are salmon boxes repeated under their masks so each objective is tied to its mask.
insights.flow: Left to right into the Q-Former, then bottom-to-top inside each tower; the image features enter cross-attention 'for every other block'; between the towers a labelled bundle (bidirectional / multimodal causal / uni-modal, the last dashed with x marks) shows the attention-masking choices.
insights.avoid: The horizontal three-line 'Attention Masking' bundle between the towers is cryptic (dashed line with x marks, a 'mutlimodal' typo) and only becomes clear after reading the right half.
